title: regional fail-safe holdoff and exponential slew-rate for tenant failovers (hotpatch)
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Hotpatch: introduce holdoff window and exponential slew-rate for regional tenant failovers to reduce cascading evictions and transient SLO violations. Default conservative settings; feature gated behind 'regional_fail_safe' flag.
description:
Motivation: During the last two incident windows we observed rapid, repeated tenant failovers across zones when a noisy upstream caused transient increases in per-tenant tail latency. The existing failover path immediately marks region-level capacity deficits and aggressively re-routes traffic which—under bursty conditions—triggered cascading evictions and amplified SLO violations. This hotpatch introduces two operational controls: (1) a short, configurable regional fail-safe holdoff window that prevents immediate tenant failover decisions from being executed repeatedly, and (2) an exponential slew-rate limiter on the rate of allowed tenant failovers per region so that the system ramps reactivations conservatively during recovery.

Summary of changes (high-level):
- Add holdoff policy evaluation in the failover orchestrator to check a region-level timestamped holdoff before acting on an SLO breach decision.
- Implement exponential slew-rate algorithm that increases the minimum interval between successive tenant failovers per region, with exponential backoff on repeated triggers and linear decay over time.
- Feature-flag the behavior behind infra feature flag 'regional_fail_safe' for staged rollout and quick revert.
- Add unit and integration tests covering holdoff interactions with the SLO enforcer and KV cache path.
- Operational runbook and helm values with suggested defaults and rollback criteria.

Checklist (implementation and rollout):
- [x] Design doc: ENG-2147 (linked)
- [x] Unit tests for holdoff and slew modules
- [x] Integration test against simulated noisy producer workload
- [x] Feature flag gating and helm chart value added
- [x] Ops runbook updated with rollback thresholds
- [x] Canary rollout to two non-prod regions, then prod staggered by region

Commit summary:
- hotpatch: add holdoff and slew-rate control in failover orchestrator
- tests: unit+integration for holdoff and slew interactions
- ops: runbook + helm values + feature flag

Changed areas (high-level files):
- serving/controller/failover_orchestrator.go — core orchestration changed to consult holdoff and slew-rate controller before triggering tenant migrations.
- serving/controller/holdoff_policy.go — new module implementing holdoff windows and bookkeeping.
- serving/controller/slew_rate_limiter.go — new module implementing exponential backoff/decay algorithm.
- serving/test/failover_policy_test.go — added coverage for transient triggers and recovery.
- infra/config/feature_flags.yaml — added 'regional_fail_safe' flag with defaults.
- ops/runbooks/regional_failover.md — operational playbook and rollback criteria.

Testing and verification steps performed:
- Local unit test suite: all green
- Integration harness: simulated noisy-producer test with controlled spike; verified reduced cascading evictions and measured 35% lower tenant-level churn vs baseline
- Canary deployment: rolled to canary (canary-1 and canary-2) for 3 hours; monitored error-rate and SLOs — no regression observed
- CI: initial perf-canary flagged a micro-regression in path latency during cold-start; optimized lock scope and re-ran canary — passed

Rollout plan and guardrails:
- Rollout via feature flag in three waves: canary -> 20% regional traffic for 30m -> 100% regionally staggered over 2 hours.
- Observability: dashboards added to Console: per-region failover-rate, per-tenant eviction count, time-since-last-failover, holdoff-trigger-count.
- Auto-rollback: if combined error-rate increase >0.5% or SLO breach >2 consecutive minutes during warmup stage, abort and revert feature flag. Ops page documents manual reversion steps.

Review notes and rationale for defaults:
- Default holdoff window: 30s. Rationale: short enough to allow reactive behavior for persistent issues, long enough to absorb short-lived spikes documented in incidents. Adjustable via helm values.
- Exponential base interval: 10s, multiplier 2x up to 5 minutes cap. Decay halflife: 5 minutes. These values were tuned in integration tests to balance availability and churn.

Review conversation (summary):
- Miguel Santos: "Question — how does holdoff interact with the SLO enforcer's immediate mitigation? Could this cause under-reaction for persistent overload?"
  Aisha (author): "Holdoff only defers the failover action; SLO enforcer still triggers local mitigations (rate-limit, preferring degraded responses). If persistent overload continues past the holdoff window, the slew-rate limiter will allow a failover but at a controlled rate. Added a unit test to validate persistent overload path."
- Evan Li: "Can we avoid additional locks in the hot path? The initial perf-canary showed a small jitter." 
  Aisha: "Addressed — reduced lock scope and added an optimistic fast-path. Updated code and re-ran perf canary; latency regression eliminated."
- Priya Menon: "Ops runbook looks good; add explicit metrics names and Grafana panel IDs." 
  Aisha: "Added exact panel refs and alert IDs to ops/runbooks/regional_failover.md."
- Miguel Santos (approval): "Approved after CI green and canary pass."

CI summary:
- ci/unit-tests: pass
- ci/integration: pass
- ci/lint: pass
- ci/perf-canary: failed on first run due to lock contention, fixed in second commit, passed on rerun
- ci/security-scan: pass

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after approvals and green CI. Tagged hotfix/2026-02-20 and notified SRE rotation. Merge note: Hotpatch should be considered safe to enable on the initial conservative defaults; ops instructed to watch per-region failover-rate metric and rollback if thresholds breached.

Operational impact: This change reduces the risk of cascading tenant evictions during transient upstream noise and should materially reduce short-lived SLO breaches caused by amplification. Behaviour is gated and revertable.
